overall: Violation found for late notice without an emergency, inaccessible open session, and improper executive session discussion; no violation on emergency labeling, Zoom access, or reconvene notice. Minutes ordered released within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Board posted notice for its March 17 executive session less than 48 hours ahead, allegedly without an emergency justifying the late notice.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board has not met its burden to show that there existed an emergency such that the Board was relieved of the requirement to post notice 48 hours, excluding weekends and holidays, prior to the March 17 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint asserted the notice should have labeled the meeting as an emergency, which the complainant said is a recommended best practice.
allegations.key_passage: we find no violation where the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body indicate on its meeting notices whether a meeting is an emergency; instead, the public body must be able to demonstrate emergency circumstances if challenged.

allegations.summary: Open session was allegedly inaccessible: notice lacked an open-session topic and the website said there was no open session business and the opening would be broadcast later.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law where the notice of its March 17 meeting failed to indicate that the Board would first meet in open session, essentially denying the public the opportunity to attend the open session.

allegations.summary: Complaint asserted the open session was inaccessible because the notice lacked a Zoom link for public access.
allegations.key_passage: where the meeting was held in person, the Board was not required to provide the public with remote access via Zoom, as the complaint asserts.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly discussed topics beyond the executive session purposes listed on the notice, including matters outside litigation strategy.
allegations.key_passage: although we find that the majority of the Board’s discussion in executive session on March 17 was improper for executive session, we find that the discussion recorded in the final substantive paragraph of the minutes related to litigation that had been threatened against the Board and therefore was proper for discussion in executive session under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: Notice allegedly failed to state whether the Board would reconvene in open session after the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We find no violation with respect to this allegation where the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body include such information on its meeting notice.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.

Release the minutes of the March 17 executive session to the public within 30 days of the letter, without redacting or withholding the portions recording inappropriate discussions; only the last substantive paragraph may be redacted if its purpose is ongoing or a privilege or Public Records exemption applies.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
